title: Agent-quality evaluation — Microsoft Foundry / AutoGen-shaped metrics (task completion, faithfulness, groundedness, coherence)
description:
The confirmed gap from the gh-pages Run #11 comparison: this repo has adopted Microsoft's *adapter shape* (PIPE-3's ContextProvider/HistoryProvider, EPIC-7) but never Microsoft's *evaluation methodology*. Grepping project-management/ for faithfulness, groundedness, coherence, task completion rate, AutoGen, and Azure AI Foundry returns zero benchmark hits — every existing suite (EPIC-6, EPIC-16, EPIC-11's TRU-3/4) measures whether the *retrieved fact is correct*, never whether the *generated response is grounded in what was actually retrieved*, *coherent once memory is injected*, or whether a *multi-step task actually completes*. Verified against two live Microsoft sources: the Foundry built-in evaluators doc (learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/concepts/built-in-evaluators, current as of this epic's creation) defines Groundedness, Coherence, Fluency, and Relevance as 1-5 LLM-judged scores, plus agent-specific Intent Resolution and Task Adherence evaluators; and the AutoGen AgentEval paper (Arabzadeh et al., 'Towards better Human-Agent Alignment: Assessing Task Utility in LLM-Powered Applications', arXiv 2402.09015) defines multi-criteria task-utility scoring (accuracy, clarity, efficiency, completeness) validated beyond binary pass/fail, plus the Pass¹/Pass⁵ terminology already confirmed from Microsoft's STATE-Bench (opensource.microsoft.com/blog/2026/05/19) in the gh-pages comparison. Note this doc's own '[Update, Aug 2026]' discipline from EPIC-11 applies here too — treat the exact evaluator names/scales as current-as-of-verification, re-check learn.microsoft.com before external-facing publication since Foundry's evaluator set has changed twice already in 2026.

AGQ-1 decides the build approach: reimplement these as native judge prompts against the SDK's existing OllamaJudge pattern (benchmarks/retrieval_quality/run.py, already proven at BENCH-1/BM-18) rather than adding `azure-ai-evaluation` as a hard dependency — this mirrors the `agent-framework` optional-extra precedent in pyproject.toml, whose own comment records the package was not reliably installable when PIPE-3 added it (2026-08-02). AGQ-2 builds task-completion-rate (the STATE-Bench-shaped Pass¹/Pass⁵ metric that has never been measured here). AGQ-3 and AGQ-4 are the two judge dimensions Microsoft's built-in evaluators define that a correct-final-answer metric cannot surface on their own: faithfulness/groundedness (is the *generated answer* actually supported by the *retrieved* context, not just correct by luck) and coherence/fluency (does injecting retrieved memory degrade response quality even when the fact is right). AGQ-5 wires all three into EPIC-17's nightly Tier 2 (LLM-judged, non-deterministic, never a PR gate — same rule BM-18/TRU-3 already follow) and into BENCHMARKS.md as a new Suite 4, feeding EPIC-20's UNI-3 scorecard. AGQ-1 blocks AGQ-2/3/4; those three are independent of each other and safe to run as parallel subagents; AGQ-5 depends on all three. Depends on EPIC-16 (BM-18, the LLM-judged run this epic adds judge passes on top of) and EPIC-11 (TRU-3's sycophancy category, a related but distinct judge dimension AGQ-3 should not duplicate).
